title: Affine algebra-module presentation from underlying quasi-coherence
statement: Let S be a scheme, A a quasi-coherent commutative O_S-algebra, and G an A-module. For every affine open U of S, if the underlying O_S-module of G restricted to U is quasi-coherent, then G restricted to the slice over U admits a presentation by coproducts of copies of A restricted to U.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0H88, proof, second paragraph; EGA I, Proposition 9.6.1

proof.text: On an affine U identify the section module M of G with an R-module and use the A(U)-action to make M a module over A(U). Present M by the free A(U)-module on all elements and relations given by the kernel. The sheafified presentation is exact because tilde preserves colimits, and compatibility of the action with restrictions makes its maps A-linear. Transport the presentation across the canonical equivalence between modules on the open subscheme and the slice site over U.

proof_origin.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0H88, proof, second paragraph; details made explicit in the worker docstring
